items.plain: While the mouse moves in a straight slow line, the ground suddenly jumps. In one case the camera went from 1 degree south to 11 degrees north in 100 ms while the mouse did not move up or down at all. In another the ground moved 8 times faster than the hand for one frame. Over all drags, the ground to mouse speed ratio is 0.6 at zoom -3 to -2, 1.4 at -1 to 0, and the 90th percentile is 4.5 (it should be about 1). Getting to a place by dragging from orbit did not converge within 40 s in 7 of 9 tries. ROUND 2 (0caf7ae): in 4 new sessions the ground to mouse ratio is 0.97 to 1.01 (p90 at most 1.22), and there were no drag overshoot windows (round 1: 19 in one session). A controlled slow drag (20 px steps, dragtest.ts) still shows single steps at zoom -2 to 1.5 where the ground moves 0 to 2.5 times the mouse (place B: zoom 0 min 0.02 max 2.4, zoom 0.5 min 0 max 2.1; place A zoom 0 to 1: 0.55 to 1.6), so the picture stutters, but no screen sized jump. Two pivot snaps of 260 and 334 px at zoom 2 to 2.3 (seeds 22, 23) were not looked at in the picture. ROUND 3 (bba983e): controlled slow drags at places B, M, R, zoom -3 to 3.5: per step ground to mouse ratio 0.55 to 1.6 everywhere (round 1 had jumps of 8 times and more), with one exception: place M at zoom 2.5 had a single step of 40 times the mouse (the ortho hand-off). ROUND 5: it still happens now and then in real sessions: seed 32 at 107 to 132 s, zoom -5.7 and -3.2, ground 145 to 287 px per 100 ms for 26 to 30 px of mouse (the whole view is replaced within two frames, a ship on the sea is in a different place each frame); seed 34 at 146 s, zoom 2.85, 1172 px for 16 px of mouse. Round 6: close to the pole at orbit zoom the whole planet turns by a large angle between two frames while the mouse barely moves (seed 42). Round 7: the jumps begin at three kinds of places. When the ground window is swapped for the next one (975 px, 363 px), when a drag passes a cube corner (432 px at zoom 3), and close to the poles. Dragging along the cube edge at 45 E is clean.
